dominant_costs_167_personas.method: cProfile of the handler thread, 167 fixture-pack-shaped personas (cloned from B3 fixture records, 8 required sources each), script profile_167_concurrent.py
dominant_costs_167_personas.persona_health: Before: 7.7 MB response; per-persona required_source_health/source_health_bindings JSON build, clone and serialisation. Removed by thin=True (response 1.93 MB, handler 0.17 s).
dominant_costs_167_personas.persona_league: ~46% of handler time was _pm12_attach_ranking_snapshot -> snapshot_record, which built the full content twice, deep-froze every item (RankingSnapshotRecord.__post_init__) and hashed evidence assertions, only to keep ranking_snapshot_id. Removed: id now built from snapshot_content_digest alone (one content pass), asserted equal to snapshot_record().ranking_snapshot_id for several periods.
dominant_costs_167_personas.persona_league_rankings: same snapshot cost (removed as above) plus N+1 per-persona get_route_policy_for_persona/get_persona_allowed_actions reads (340 calls for 167 personas), removed by passing include_route_policy/health/allowed_actions=False.
dominant_costs_167_personas.persona_fleet: No single item dominates: _pm12_persona_league_rows 0.128 s, per-row projection (_project_persona_fleet_row_impl 0.109 s), quarterly ranking items 0.049 s; it also called _pm12_attach_ranking_snapshot (line 7204), so it gets the snapshot saving. Its before p95 above 2 s in the concurrent run was GIL contention with the 7.7 MB persona-health response.
dominant_costs_167_personas.not_reproduced: Hosted store round-trip latency is not reproduced; local stores are in-process.
